title: Calibration campaign conductor: run orchestration, artifact lifecycle, and validator hooks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a reusable "conductor" in the Redwood Console to schedule, orchestrate, and govern quantization calibration campaigns (FP8/INT8) with first-class artifacts, retention rules, role-based access, and automated accuracy validation hooks.

Scope:
- Scheduling: allow users to define campaigns (collections of calibration runs) with recurrence, priority, and target model variants.
- Orchestration: job router that assigns runs to calibration workers (hosted/dedicated/private), supports preemption/fallback, and records run lineage.
- Artifacts: standardized artifact manifest for per-run outputs (histograms, scale tables, per-layer stats, metrics, quant-profile blobs) stored in our artifact store with TTL and lifecycle tags.
- Retention & GC: UI and backend controls for retention policy per project and campaign; soft-delete + reclaim pipeline with idempotent GC worker.
- Permissions: map Console RBAC roles to artifact-level ACLs (owner/editor/viewer), support cross-team shareable read-only artifact links, and audit logs for exports.
- Accuracy validation: integrate validator hooks that run the post-calibration evaluation suite (predefined eval sets), produce pass/fail gating, regression deltas, and optional automatic rollback/flagging.

Non-goals: automatic model conversion; deep runtime kernel selection (handled by runtime team).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Users can create a campaign via Console or API that spawns N runs with configurable schedule and high/low priority.
2) Each run produces a JSON manifest with artifact URIs and metadata (run_id, campaign_id, model_version, quant_mode).
3) Artifacts honor project-level TTLs; GC removes expired artifacts and surfaces audit events.
4) Validator hooks run automatically after calibration; failures set campaign state to "needs-attention" and surface a diff dashboard.
5) RBAC enforced: only users in owner/editor roles can delete artifacts; read-only links for cross-team review do not permit artifact export by default.
6) Migration path exists for legacy calibration artifacts to new manifest format (migration job with dry-run).

Technical approach (high level):
- Backend: new "conductor" service owned by calibration-platform team. Stores campaign/run state in CampaignRuns table (run_id, campaign_id, status, worker_id, started_at, completed_at, manifest_uri, ttl, created_by).
- Artifacts: use existing object store + artifact-index (add artifact-type and layer-level tags); manifests stored in S3 path with prefix /calibration/{campaign}/{run_id}/manifest.json.
- GC: periodic GC worker that lists manifests past TTL and moves objects to quarantine bucket for 7d soft-delete before hard-delete; each step emits audit events to console-audit topic.
- Validator hooks: pluggable containerized jobs that run against a canonical eval harness, emit results to run manifest and call Console API to update run state.
- UX: Console campaign creation flow with templated eval sets, retention TTL dropdown, RBAC selector, and a campaign timeline view that links to artifacts and validation diffs.

Risks & mitigation:
- Large artifact sizes: enforce per-run size budget and autosplit for layer artifacts; prefer compressed histograms.
- Data leakage: require KMS encryption at rest and ensure cross-team shareables are tokenized and time-limited.
- Orchestration failures: retry/backoff and automatic fallback to compatible runtime variants.

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha behind feature flag for internal tenants (QA + infra owners).
2) Beta with 3 pilot customers and dedicated monitoring for artifact growth and validator runtimes.
3) GA after 2 weeks of stable runs and sign-off from security/compliance.

Monitoring & observability:
- Metrics: run success/failure rate, avg validator runtime, artifact bytes/day, GC throughput, TTL misses.
- Dashboards: run-level timeline, campaign health, and accuracy regression heatmap.

comments: 2025-02-20 - Initial scoping session with Eng (Sofia), Runtime (Liam), and Security (Priya). Decided conductor should not manage hardware placement; runtime will provide a placement API.
2025-02-27 - Design review: added artifact manifest versioning and a migration plan for legacy artifacts. Action: PM to draft migration job spec.
2025-03-01 - Engineering spike: Ravi's team validated manifest layout and benchmarked validator container startup time (median 11s cold). PR created: platform#4211.
2025-03-03 - Security review (Priya): KMS required for artifacts; recommend tokenized share links and 7-day default soft-delete quarantine. Security approved with minor comments.

2025-03-04 - UX feedback (Maya): need clearer TTL explanation and default to project-level retention; added 'archive' action in timeline UX. UX mock link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/Cal-Conductor-Mocks.

2025-03-05 - Found a regression in the validator harness where certain FP8 profiles produced NaNs in one eval; incident logged and isolated to preprocessing (ticket ENG-40807). Next: add preflight checks to validator.
Next steps: finalize API contract with runtime team, implement migration dry-run job, and wire up the validator runner to the campaign lifecycle.
